$description:
Component tier — the override surface.

Every token here resolves to a semantic token, never to a primitive. That is enforced by the build, not by review: a component token pointing at {ref.red.700} would silently ignore a brand override on exactly the value a brand most needs to control.

Why this tier exists at all, and why it matters more here than it would at a platform vendor: ZoBlocks ships source into the customer's repository. Without an override point, 'customise the badge' means 'edit the copied file', and an edited file can never receive an upstream fix. Every fork is a component that silently stops being maintained. This tier is what keeps customisation and the upgrade channel compatible.

Because these resolve to semantic tokens, they follow light, dark and high-contrast automatically. A component token needs a per-theme value only when it must break from the semantic it normally tracks — which so far, nothing does.

badge.$description: StatusBadge. The shared severity chip — critical must read identically on a lab result, a medication and an allergy, which is why every component routes severity through this one set rather than styling its own.

accordion.$description: Accordion / Disclosure. Two groups here are load-bearing rather than decorative. The severity rail is the only signal that survives a collapsed section, so it routes through the same status set as StatusBadge — critical must read identically on a lab result, a medication, and a chart section. And restricted is drawn from flag.*, not from the status scale, because it describes the record's legal standing rather than a measurement; rendering it as merely disabled would tell a reader the section is unavailable when it is actually withheld.

alert.$description: AlertBanner. Severity tiers are an interruption budget — only critical may take focus. The tokens are separate from badge so a product can make an inline badge quiet without also making a critical interruption quiet.

value.$description: ClinicalValue. The unit is deliberately a separate colour from the number — it is context, not the reading — but both live in one element so they cannot drift apart under truncation or wrapping.

absent.$description: AbsentValue. Absence is rendered as a statement, never as a blank or a dash, so it gets real typographic weight rather than being styled out of the way.

range.$description: ReferenceRange. The band is the normal interval; the marker is where this result fell. Both are overridable because the visual weight between them is the one thing customers reliably want to tune.

banner.$description: PatientBanner. Persistent identity header. Restricted and deceased states change the whole bar rather than adding a chip to it, because an identity header that looks normal for a restricted record is the failure this component exists to prevent.

surface-card.$description: Shared by every card-shaped clinical component — medication, appointment, coverage. One set rather than three so a customer restyling 'cards' changes cards, not one of them.

field.$description: Shared by every input — dose, quantity, ratio, identifier, and the questionnaire renderer's controls. Invalid is a border-and-text change rather than a background wash, so it survives forced-colors mode.

prefilled-bg.$description: A prefilled answer is marked, not hidden. A clinician signing a form does not always notice which values were carried forward, and an unmarked prefill is a signature on data nobody re-read.

switch.$description:
Switch — the binary control, and the override surface for its geometry as well as its colour.

Two things here are unusual and deliberate.

`target-min` is the hit area, and it is a SEPARATE token from `track-w`/`track-h`. That decoupling is what lets a 26x14px switch sit in a dense flowsheet row while keeping a 44px target: shrinking the pill must never shrink the target, because a mis-tap on a clinical flag is not a cosmetic defect.

`track-off-bg` resolves to {border-strong} rather than a light grey. The off track IS the control's boundary, so SC 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 against the page — and the conventional rgba(0,0,0,0.25) treatment lands near 1.9:1. The pair is in the contrast gate.

On/off track luminance is close enough that colour alone cannot carry the state, which is why the component renders thumb position, a thumb glyph and a text state word as well. These tokens are the fourth signal, never the first.

track-off-bg.$description: Also the control's boundary — see the group description.

track-caution-bg.$description: tone="caution" — an on-state that removes a safety net reads amber, not brand green.

track-critical-bg.$description: tone="critical" — an on-state that suppresses a clinical check.

track-neutral-bg.$description: tone="neutral" — a view preference with no clinical direction.

label-off-fg.$description: The off track is {border-strong}, not the accent — a mid-grey in every theme. This pointed at {text-on-accent}, which follows the accent, and the dark accent is light: the off word rendered #071014 on #5d6c7e at 3.57:1 and shipped.

pad.$description: Gap between the thumb and the track edge. Travel is computed from this, never hard-coded.

target-min.$description: The hit area — see the group description. Decoupled from track-w/track-h on purpose.

hold-ms.$description: Hold-to-confirm duration. A host may set this to 0ms to disable the hold entirely in favour of the dialog path — holding is a timed input and SC 2.2.1 applies, so it must be removable without a fork.

chart.$description:
ObservationTrend, Flowsheet and ClinicalScale.

These exist as tokens rather than hard-coded SVG attributes for a specific reason: a chart is the one surface where the reader cannot re-read a mislabelled value, so the axis, grid and band weights have to be tunable per product without editing the drawing code.

The status hues are NOT re-declared here. A point that is high on a chart uses the same amber as a badge that says high, because a colour that means something in a table and something else in a graph on the same screen is worse than no colour at all.

point-radius-flagged.$description: An out-of-range point is larger as well as differently shaped and differently coloured. Three redundant encodings, because this is the mark a reader is scanning for.

nav.$description: ContextBar, SectionNav and ClinicalBreadcrumb. Current-section state carries a border as well as a background, so it survives forced-colors mode where background-color is discarded.

cs.$description: ClinicalStatus. Two chip heights and the glyph size, exposed as tokens because density is the one thing a host reasonably re-scales — a ward workstation runs denser than a tablet at the bedside. The tones are not here: they route through the shared status family so that critical reads identically on a chip, a rail and a row.

rv.$description: ResultValue. The two value sizes, exposed because a results grid and a chart panel want different ones and the difference is not density in general — it is how large a number has to be before a clinician trusts they read it correctly.

risk.$description: RiskIndicator. One token: how large the numeral is. Exposed because the band is the honest resolution and the numeral is a convenience, and a deployment that wants the convenience quieter should be able to have it without forking the component.

presence.$description: CareTeamPresence. One token: the avatar diameter. Exposed because presence sits beside a patient's name in a header on one screen and inside a co-presence stack on another, and the ring geometry is drawn relative to it — scaling the avatar is the supported way to move between the two without forking the stylesheet.

chart-header.$description: ChartHeader. One token: the tone bar on a safety fact. It is a colour rather than a dimension because the strip's whole restraint is that the bar is the only coloured pixel in the row — a deployment that wants a house palette for severity changes this and nothing else, and cannot accidentally turn six facts into six filled chips.

stack.$description: RecentPatientStack. One token: the fallback chart accent, used by the eighth slot and by any chart whose hash lands outside the palette. The other seven route through the status and flag families rather than a new palette, so a brand override reaches them and none can drift into a hue a clinical severity already owns.

datetime.$description:
DateField, Calendar, DatePicker, BirthDateField, TimeField, SessionTimeField and ClinicalDateTime.

The input chrome is deliberately absent: these components spend the shared `field.*` tokens, so a date field and a dose field cannot drift apart in a customer's theme. What is here is the surface a calendar and a session triple add on top — the grid cell, the selected and range fills, and the held/derived pair.

`held` is the one that carries meaning rather than decoration. Start, end and duration are three values with two degrees of freedom, and which one the user asserted has to be visible or the next edit is a surprise. It resolves to the accent family because it marks the value the user owns, not a status.

cell-muted-fg.$description: Adjacent-month and unavailable days. Not `text-subtle`: at the 4.5:1 floor the subtle step fails on the overlay ground a bottom sheet paints, and a day a user can still reach is not exempt.

cell-hover-bg.$description: The transient tint under the pointer. `accent-wash`, not `bg-muted`: the neutral ramp is blue-biased slate, and a slate cell inside a green selection reads as a different system rather than as a weaker state of the same one.

cell-range-bg.$description: The committed band. One step above the hover and the provisional preview, because a range that is chosen and a range that is being pointed at must not paint the same.

today-marker.$description: A dot under the numeral as well as a weight change, because today must survive greyscale like every other state in the library.

held-fg.$description: The member of a session triple the user asserted. Paired with a lock glyph and the word `Held`, so the badge is never colour alone.

cell-size.$description: The visible cell. The hit area is the whole grid track and is floored at the density target, so clinical density tightens the type and the gaps and never the target.

target.$description: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8. Follows the density profile, which itself clamps at 24px.

rec-ring.$description: The ring round a recommended day. A decorative swatch rather than a status, because a recommendation guides and carries no clinical meaning; the ring's shape and the reason in the cell's name are the channels that do not depend on hue.

rec-bg.$description: The `fill` treatment of a recommended day.

rec-mark.$description: The sparkle on a recommended day in the `icon` treatment.

rec-mark-inverse.$description: The sparkle beside "Why this date?" on the inverse tooltip surface.

event-warning.$description: The default event bar under a day's numeral. Bars, not dots, so an event is never read as the today dot or the availability dots that share the strip.

tip-bg.$description: The day tooltip's surface: the inverse of the page, so it reads as floating over the grid rather than as part of it.

tip-check.$description: The ticks under a recommendation's reason, on the inverse surface — the border step, because the foreground step is tuned for the page ground, not its inverse.

recorder.$description: Recorder. Every value here resolves through a semantic token so a brand override reaches it; `rec` routes to status.recording, which exists so the capture tell is not the same red as an alarm.

rec-ink.$description: The tell's LABEL, not its dot. Text owes 4.5:1 and the recording red is tuned for a dot, so the label borrows the darker critical step rather than failing quietly at 10px.

wave-off.$description: The unplayed half of a take is the shape a reader aims at before clicking, so it is solved against the pane rather than faded toward it. text-muted already carries small text on this ground, which is a stricter bar than the 3:1 a non-text mark owes.

lane-h.$description: Lane height. Below about 40px the peak buckets stop being readable as a shape and the art should fall back to strip.

menu.$description: ChartContextMenu. Structural only: the four consequence tiers resolve through the existing status ramp (text-muted, accent, status-high, status-restricted), so no new colour pair enters the contrast gate. The subject header is a surface rather than a row and must read as inert in every theme — in forced-colors its background is discarded, which is why it carries a border as well as a tint.
